J U D G M E N T / AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)

1. This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the LAC no. 155/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mam Chand Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 18 Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.

per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been LAC no.
155/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Mam Chand Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 18 observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.

sentences.text: The market value of the acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".
It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 06.02.2006, however,
physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment,
therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has LAC no. 155/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW))
Mam Chand Vs. Union of India Page no. 9 of 18 been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.

sentences.text: Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value,

sentences.text: (vi) The learned LAC has also made grave error by not calling the petitioners for negotiation and the decision has been taken arbitrarily which is against the principles of natural justice.
The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 23 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Mubarakpur Dabas and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI LAC no. 155/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mam Chand Vs.
Union of India Page no. 11 of 18 Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e.
water, electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to NH8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award.

(ix) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by the said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however,
the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.
It is and infringement of right of property as laid down in Article 300, that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

11. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.

I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under : 
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?OPP 16.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
17. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Ajit Singh (supra).

18. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.

An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).

opennyai_summary.facts:
1. This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.
opennyai_summary.issue:
7. As such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) The learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under : 
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?OPP 16.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.
It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects and has assessed the market value after considering the level of development, locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.
The Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land by adopting the indicative price fixed by the government of NCT of Delhi @ Rs. 15,70,000 per acre for the year 2001 - 2002, which is applicable with effect from 01.04.2001.
9.
It is submitted that the ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view the aspects enumerated under Section 23 and 24 of the Act.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld. Counsel for the respondents have submitted LAC no. 155/ 2016 (Award No. 25/2005 06/DC(NW)) Mam Chand Vs. Union of India Page no. 15 of 18 that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 459 of 2016, Ajit Singh Vs. Union of India.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.
(v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.
The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.
The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 22.
As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 6//6 min (002), 15/1 (014) and 6//6 (400) has not LAC no. 155/ 2016 (Award No. 25/2005 06/DC(NW)) Mam Chand Vs. Union of India Page no. 17 of 18 been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.
23. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
24.
The petitioner shall not be entitled for interest from the period w.e.f.
07.01.2018 i.e. the date of death of petitioner Mam Chand till 22.04.2019 i.e. the date when the application U/o XXII Rule 2 and 3 CPC was filed, as mentioned in order dated 10.07.2019.
25.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
